हॉलीवुड एक्टर मार्क बेनिंगटन ने लखनऊ से इंस्पायर होकर अपनी नई शॉर्ट फिल्म Dear Tillo बनाई है! 🎬
मार्क बेनिंगटन का कहना है कि उनकी इस शॉर्ट फिल्म का बीज लखनऊ में ही पड़ा था। 🌰
उन्होंने पिछले साल ही इस फिल्म की शूटिंग की थी और विंटर में एडिट और साउंड डिज़ाइन पूरा किया। 💻
शिकागो, टोरंटो, मुंबई और पुणे के बाद अब यह फिल्म Lucknow Film Festival में दिखाई गई। 🌍
पुणे में फिल्म को बेस्ट एक्टर का अवॉर्ड भी मिला है और अब यह जयपुर जाएगी। 🏆
इसमें मार्क ने एक US के रेगुलर प्रोफेसर का रोल निभाया है जो इंडिया आता है। 🇮🇳
लेकिन लखनऊ के ऑडियंस को लेकर उनका कहना है कि इस बार स्क्रीनिंग के दौरान लोग बातें कर रहे थे और वीडियो कॉल भी कर रहे थे जो काफी डिस्ट्रैक्टिंग था। 📱
आपको क्या लगता है, फिल्म स्क्रीनिंग के दौरान ऑडियंस का ऐसा बर्ताव कितना सही है? 💬

ctx.title: Mark Bennington turns writer-director with Dear Tillo, says the seed of the short film was born in Lucknow
ctx.summary: American actor Mark Bennington says his connection with Lucknow has shaped new avenues. He recently wrote and directed short film Dear Tillo where he acted too
ctx.text:
American actor Mark Bennington says he has visited Lucknow only twice, but his connection with the city has shaped new avenues. The Heeramandi actor says that his visit inspired him to make the short film Dear Tillo , with which he turned writer, director, and producer.
On his recent visit, to participate in Lucknow Film Festival Season 4, he says, “It’s a film that actually happened because of my previous visit to Lucknow as a jury member. I saw so many short films and it kind of gave me an idea of what I would do if I were to ever make a short film? It inspired me to make a universally themed film that is easy to watch, with which the audience could relate to, and has a little twist at the end. So, the seed of this short film was born in Lucknow.”
Recently seen in Vibes and Operation Safed Sagar , Bennington says he shot for the film last year. “Last winter I did the whole edit and sound design, everything. And then this year, started submitting it to the film festivals. We had our world premiere in Chicago South Asian Film Festival, at International Film Festival South Asia Toronto, then Mumbai and in Pune where we got the best actor award. After Lucknow, we are going to Jaipur, the Indian festival in Florence. It is slowly making its way around the globe.”
Working on his own project gave him the opportunity to explore something different from what he is offered.
“Nobody has ever seen me in a role like this because I play a regular guy, a professor from the United States who’s come to India for the first time searching for his former student."
He adds, “They meet again, and he realises that the life he had imagined for her is very different from the one she is actually leading. That’s where the story unfolds. He arrives with a certain expectation, only to discover that reality is quite different from what he had envisioned. That’s what makes it interesting!”
On his experience in Lucknow he says, “This time I noticed a change. Two years back, during the screening, it was a pretty respectable audience that was quietly watching and intent and listening. But, this time, people were having full conversations while someone was even doing a video call which was quite distracting. Even during the question and answer session it continued. There's only so many times you can tell somebody to be quiet. But, anyways, I watched some nice films, so it was a mixed experience.” He film was showcased in the Beyond Borders in the international film section.
Deep Saxena writes on Bollywood, OTT, television, food and culture for the daily Entertainment & Lifestyle supplement, HT City.
